review_type: Authored legal-model audit with official-source quote checks and offline counterexamples; not independent legal certification

findings.title: Input labels were overclaiming legal conclusions
findings.analysis: Purpose, agreement status, GDPR roles, biometrics, and country flags now provide partial hints. Negative inference requires an explicit exhaustive mapping. HIPAA role classifications still settle the exact capacity asserted under the request trust model.

findings.title: Route labels omitted important statutory qualifications
findings.analysis: All routes have substantive core statements. Necessity, consent validity, subsidiary derogations, public-register restrictions, research exceptions and procedural qualifications are included. The evaluator uses full core statements rather than treating labels as legal tests.

findings.title: HIPAA permissions confused covered entities and business associates
findings.analysis: Covered-entity routes are capacity-scoped. A business associate requires its own 164.502(a)(3)-(4)/164.504(e) authority. Recipient safeguards also distinguish the two capacities. A business-associate classification alone does not prove the recipient acts for this sender.

findings.title: Unmodelled and open route sets could produce excessive certainty
findings.analysis: An unmodelled placeholder cannot establish permission; failure of every represented route in an open list stays undetermined. HIPAA permissions and Irish research alternatives are explicitly open.

findings.title: Statutory exceptions were omitted or entangled with unrelated route scope
findings.analysis: Minimum-necessary exceptions now cover all six 164.502(b)(2) categories independently of sender capacity. Article 35(10) and Article 9(2)(a) proviso have exception nodes. HIPAA Security Rule has an electronic-PHI scope.

findings.title: Irish research safeguards were treated as the Article 9 research basis
findings.analysis: DPA 2018 s. 54 with s. 42 is the selected 9(2)(j) basis. Health Research Regulations are additional safeguards, reachable separately through the Article 9(4) condition, including when explicit consent is the selected Article 9 route.

findings.title: Failure of one Irish implementation ruled out an entire GDPR opening
findings.analysis: A successful selected enabling law supplies the opening. Failure leaves it unknown because other national/Union law or the 9(2)(h) contract alternative may exist. For an additional safeguard, an established failure remains adverse and an out-of-scope duty is satisfied conditionally.

findings.title: Printed HIPAA text includes a largely vacated rule
findings.analysis: Dated HHS notice is prepended to affected source bundles. This corrects source presentation but is not a machine-enforced operative-law filter. A decision relying on the affected rule still needs operative-law review.

findings.title: Answers are not keyed by actor and processing operation
findings.analysis: One node has one answer for the whole request. Establishment, legal basis, consent and necessity may differ across sender, recipient, disclosure, receipt and reuse. Full statements now warn about scope, but the data model cannot represent all those independent assessments. Needs an explicit assessment-unit design and regression scenarios before a multi-actor correctness claim.

findings.title: Legal coverage is deliberately incomplete
findings.analysis: Irish health-research measures are reachable through the special-category item; non-special-category personal-data health research is not reliably reached. Irish transitional/special-sector measures, HIPAA special scope exclusions, state law and other regimes remain incomplete. Either add coverage or define explicit unsupported-case boundaries before freezing.

findings.title: Source validity and LLM entailment are different checks
findings.analysis: Quotation and fact-pointer validators establish that text exists, not that a cited fact establishes every part of a bundled legal test. Many provisions remain bundled. No exhaustive human legal sign-off or live-model evaluation was performed. Needs a reviewed case set with expected condition answers.

findings.title: Currency and interpretation are not fully versioned
findings.analysis: Official snapshots support provenance. The offline HIPAA source is the 2025 annual CFR; current eCFR and HHS notice were inspected separately. Irish revised text reports changes known in force through 2026-09-17. Guidance/case law and later amendments have not all received a full retained-document review. A freeze must specify an as-of date, source versions and invalidation procedure.

findings.title: Some edges express implementation policy, not statutory statements
findings.analysis: Intake bindings, regime gates, shared-node dependencies, route-not-claimed closure, advisory classification and standing-activity treatment are authored system choices. Five relatedMatch links retrieve analogous concepts only. None imports one regime’s definition or creates a legal permission.

requirements.review: Articles 2-3 and definitions. Material exclusions and actor-specific establishment/offering/monitoring tests are in the core. One party’s establishment cannot settle the other’s. The aggregate gate is a remaining modelling limit.

Articles 26/28. Joint determination and processing on behalf of the other party are relational facts. Terms, sufficient guarantees and subprocessor conditions are bundled; an arrangement status alone is insufficient.

Six Article 6(1) alternatives retained. Necessary processing, valid consent and legitimate-interest balancing are explicit. Article 6(3) bases and public-authority exception retained; actor-specific bases cannot yet coexist independently.

Ten Article 9(2) alternatives retained. Article 9(3) secrecy and law openings are conjuncts. Consent proviso and national additional conditions are represented. Biometrics require the identification purpose. Irish non-special-category research remains outside this path.

Articles 44-49. Core statements include subsidiarity and 49(2)/(6) conditions, with 49(3) exceptions. Chapter V transfer is not equivalent to an EEA geography flag. Adequacy and safeguard effectiveness require case-specific, current evaluation; guidance is not a quoted statute edge.

Article 89(1) requires minimisation and safeguards, shared with 9(2)(j), and does not supply a standalone Article 6 or 9 basis. The native Irish research requirement must also be reached for ordinary personal-data health research, which remains a coverage gap.

Article 35 and Recital 91. Individual-practitioner scale is not a universal exemption. Article 35(10) is an explicit exception; the DPIA core includes content, consultation and review. Existing-activity nonblocking treatment is policy, not an exemption enacted by Article 35.

Article 32 requires risk-appropriate organisational and technical measures for the relevant actor. Encryption alone does not settle the duty. Advisory catalogue treatment does not make the statutory obligation optional.

Articles 5, 12-14 and 30. Applicable transparency exceptions, rights qualifications and the narrow small-organisation record exemption are in full statements. Individual rights and several controller duties are not exhaustively encoded. Standing/advisory treatment is policy.

160.103 and 164.500/502/514. Complete covered-entity definition restored, PHI/de-identification distinct from permission. Either-party applicability is a retrieval gate, not a rule imposing every duty on both parties. Special scope exclusions remain a boundary.

164.502, 506, 508, 510, 512, 514. Covered-entity permissions now scoped, BA authority separate. Route cores incorporate relevant qualifications; open placeholders cannot establish permission. Special restrictions and operative law still require judgment.

164.502(e), 504(e), 514(e). BA and subcontractor assurances are relational, including alternatives/exceptions. DUA arises when relying on the LDS permission. The LDS route cannot bypass DUA by asserting that its own reliance scope is false.

164.502(b) and 514(d). All six statutory exception categories represented as independent scope predicates. Treatment exception is disclosure to/request by a provider for treatment, not a general research/payment/operations exception.

164.302-316. Electronic PHI scope and physical/technical/administrative/documentation requirements included. Addressable does not mean optional without assessment. Catalogue advisory status is policy. Broader security coverage remains bundled.

164.530(c) applies to covered entities; BA safeguards follow 164.504(e) and applicable direct duties. These are separately scoped. Receipt by a US organisation does not by itself settle either capacity.

DPA 2018 s. 38(1)(a)-(b), subject to necessity/proportionality. Includes administering non-statutory schemes rooted in a statutory/constitutional function. The actual controller function still needs its own law; this is one supporting national basis.

DPA 2018 s. 52. Necessity for a listed purpose, practitioner responsibility and suitable/specific measures are conjuncts. Article 9(3) confidentiality remains a separate GDPR condition. Failure of s. 52 does not exclude every other basis.
DPA 2018 s. 53. Necessity for the specified public-health interest and suitable/specific measures are required together. A public-health purpose label is not the complete test.

SI 314/2018 as amended by SI 188/2019 and SI 18/2021. Current explicit consent, declaration, chart review and deferred consent requirements are qualified. Governance, ethics and data-protection assessment are conjuncts. Transitional placeholder and coverage are open; these measures are not a standalone GDPR legal basis.

DPA 2018 ss. 54 and 42. Necessity/proportionality and section 42 safeguards, including minimisation and identifiable-data limits, are separate conjuncts. Additional health-research measures do not disappear when this basis is used.

mapping_review.rule: relatedMatch means a useful comparison only. GDPR personal data and HIPAA PHI have different scope; pseudonymised data and LDS are not equivalent; consent and authorization are not interchangeable.

acceptance_before_freeze: Key each substantive assessment by actor and processing operation, or enforce and test a narrower supported case contract.
Resolve the Irish ordinary-personal-data research path and define supported HIPAA scope exclusions.
Complete an as-of legal-status and guidance review with retained versioned evidence.
Review expected answers and conclusions for the 15 scenarios, plus counterexamples, with legal expertise; run the case suite.
Explicitly approve policy choices such as advisory and standing-activity treatment.
